# Report: Does Drinking Boiled Garlic Water Cure COVID-19?

## Conclusion

**The claim is false.** There is no scientific evidence that drinking boiled garlic water cures COVID-19. Multiple fact-checking organizations, health authorities, and the World Health Organization have debunked this claim.

## Evidence

The claim that boiled garlic water cures COVID-19 originated in viral social media posts, particularly a message attributed to an unnamed "old Chinese doctor" from Wuhan. FactCheck.org investigated and found this claim to be false, noting there was no cure for the virus at the time the claim circulated in early 2020.

While garlic does contain compounds like allicin that show some antimicrobial and antiviral properties in laboratory (test tube) studies, there is no clinical data from human trials demonstrating that garlic water prevents, treats, or cures COVID-19. The AAP FactCheck noted that a Doherty Institute study showing garlic reduced viral infectiousness was conducted only in test tubes, not in humans, and the institute stated the study doesn't show garlic has any medical applications.

The World Health Organization explicitly addressed COVID-19 misinformation, stating there is no licensed medication to cure COVID-19 and pushing back against bogus cure claims. The Mayo Clinic similarly categorized unverified remedies not recommended by healthcare professionals as myths.

## Why the Belief Persists

Garlic has a legitimate reputation for general antimicrobial and immune-boosting properties, which may lead people to assume it works against COVID-19. However, lab-demonstrated antiviral activity does not translate to clinical efficacy in humans without proper trials.
